summary: Werner Thomas was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied under Emil Sieg and Wolfgang Krause (~1946–1952) and held a post at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1964–1989).
Wes Borton works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at East Carolina University, under Derek F. Maher, and at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

Whalen Lai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at International Christian University and Harvard (Ph.D. ~1975), later teaching at the University of Illinois (~1975–1978) and UC Davis (~1978–2010).
Whitelaw Ainslie was an Indologist who served as an Assistant Surgeon (1788) and Surgeon (1794–1815) for the East India Company. In 1829, he became a Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh.

Whitley Stokes was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at St Columba's College, earned a B.A. from Trinity College Dublin (1846–1851), and studied under Carl Siegfried and Rudolf Thomas Siegfried.

Whitney Cox is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Virginia and the University of Chicago (PhD 1998–2006 under Sheldon Pollock and others), holding faculty posts at SOAS (~2006–2013) and Chicago (~2013).

Widi Widiyanto specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Sekolah Tinggi Agama Buddha Maha Prajna and Universitas Hindu Indonesia (Dr 2022–2025), becoming a Dosen Tetap at STIAB Jinarakkhita in 2022.

Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. Educated at the University of Ceylon and SOAS (Ph.D. ~1956), he held posts at the University of Ceylon (1952–1973), Peradeniya (1964), and Kelaniya (~1957–1986).

Wiktor Jan Porzeziński was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Moscow State University (Dr. 1892–1903) under Filipp Fortunatov. He held academic posts at Moscow State University (1903–1921), University of Warsaw (~1921–1929), and John Paul II Catholic University.
Wilber Theodore Elmore was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln by 1915 and taught at Palmer Theological Seminary in 1925.

Wilbur Stone Deming was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Brown and Boston Universities, joined the American Marathi Mission in 1912, and served as Superintendent at American Mission High School, Ahmednagar in 1924.
Wilburn Hansen works in religious studies and Japanology. He pursued graduate studies at the University of Colorado Boulder and Stanford University, studying under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

Wilfred Cantwell Smith was a religious studies scholar educated at Toronto, Cambridge, and Princeton. He taught at Forman Christian College (1940–1946) and held professorships and directorships at McGill University (1948–1951) and Harvard University (1964–1973; 1978–1985).

Wilfred Harvey Schoff specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Harvard and the University of Pennsylvania, he served at the Philadelphia Commercial Museum (1900) and was a visiting lecturer at Wisconsin-Madison (1901) and Illinois (1903).

Wilfrid Sellars was a philosopher who studied at Michigan, Buffalo, and Oxford. He taught at the Universities of Iowa (1938–1946) and Minnesota (1947–1958), Yale University (1958–1963), and the University of Pittsburgh (1963–1989).
Wilfried Nölle was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen under Helmuth von Glasenapp from approximately 1947 to 1950.

Wilhelm Alexander Unkrig was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kazan Theological Academy (1908). He served as a librarian at the Anthropos Institute and Leiden University, later lecturing at Goethe University Frankfurt (1943).

Wilhelm Brandenstein was an Austrian linguist and Indologist. After studying at Innsbruck and Vienna (Ph.D. ~1925) under scholars including Paul Kretschmer, he spent his academic career at the University of Graz, directing its comparative linguistics institute (1941–1967).

Wilhelm Cartellieri was an Indologist who studied at the Universities of Leipzig and Vienna (Ph.D. 1878–1884) under Georg Bühler. He completed his Habilitation (1899) and served as an associate professor (1902) at the University of Innsbruck.

Wilhelm Deecke was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Berlin and Leipzig (Dr. phil. ~1870) under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He worked primarily as a school administrator, directing institutions in Lübeck, Strasbourg, Bouxwiller, and Mulhouse.
